statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity index futures remain shut with the 22:00 UTC restart under two hours away, so there is no live Nasdaq-100 price path to score and Tail stays far below the block threshold, while Stress holds elevated on a verified weekend missile exchange between Iran and US Navy warships, a pending Iranian prohibited zone near the Strait of Hormuz and September FOMC hike pricing above half heading into CPI week.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the whole outlook; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: No live Nasdaq-100 price path under two hours before the 22:00 UTC reopen, after a verified Iran-US Navy missile exchange and with an Iranian prohibited zone near Hormuz still pending
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range against a 29,482.30 previous close, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold. VIX ended at 14.53 (+1.47%) after a contained 13.80-14.58 range, which is not a stressed equity-volatility regime. Friday's internals were rotational rather than directional, with semiconductors higher while several megacaps fell, and that split argues against an aligned one-way regime being carried into the reopen. The geopolitical picture is now a verified two-way kinetic exchange rather than rhetoric alone. The IRGC said its Aerospace Force fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer it accused of harassing Iranian vessels and enforcing the naval blockade, claiming both were damaged and withdrew; CENTCOM said both warships evaded the attacks with no US personnel harmed, and that US forces then struck three Iranian crude tankers, having separately sunk the M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman. Alongside that, Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran will declare a prohibited zone in the coming days, beginning at the US Navy blockade line and extending into parts of the Gulf, with any vessel entering placed on Iran's sanctions list, and said passage maps agreed with Oman will be signed shortly. The zone has been signalled but not yet declared, which is why it sits in conditional drivers rather than in observed evidence. OPEC+ met on Sunday and left October quotas unchanged, pausing its unwinding of the 1.65 million barrel-per-day cut after six consecutive increases, and next meets on October 4. Brent settled Friday at $96.28 (+0.80%) and WTI at $91.48 (+0.20%), with crude up roughly 8-9% on the week on Hormuz supply risk. On rates, H.15 for September 3 shows the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, and a stronger-than-expected August payroll print has left market-implied odds of a September 15-16 FOMC hike above half. That combination keeps Stress elevated. It does not move Tail, because Tail measures an observed pathological price path and no price path exists while the venue is shut. Conditional risk is therefore concentrated in the 22:00-02:00 UTC reopen, when a two-day headline backlog would meet the thinnest depth of the week; that window maps to WATCH rather than to a block, since gap risk without observed extension after a failed retracement is not evidence of mean-reversion failure. Monday is the US Labor Day holiday: US cash markets are closed, CME equity index futures trade a shortened session ending 17:00 UTC, and the US data calendar is empty until Tuesday. The week's high-impact checkpoints are PPI and Oracle results on September 10 and CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC that sits outside this outlook window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held a flat 5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress oscillated between 52 and 59 across the weekend closure, easing through the Asian overnight and firming steadily across the European and US Sunday hours to finish the window at its high of 59. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour, reflecting a closed venue rather than an observed regime.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover two further closed hours, the scheduled 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday with no US cash open inside the window. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the two hours around the reopen, which reach 23 and 21 and map to WATCH where the verified Iran-US Navy exchange, a signalled but undeclared Iranian prohibited zone and a stretched energy complex would meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 9 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 68 at the reopen on the combined rates, energy and geopolitical backdrop before unwinding toward 49 once futures halt for the holiday break at 17:00 UTC. No US macro release falls inside the window, and the next high-impact checkpoints are PPI on September 10 and CPI on September 11.
